description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Round 7. Verify the round-6 fixes (commit 184ba12): the rebuilt theme guard (three invariants in src/app/theme-source.test.ts), the lint rule Intl handling (with and without new, formatter methods, ListFormat), and the container-smoke dirty flag. Check against the spec delta and design.md. Do NOT re-report what design.md lists under "Accepted limits (review round 3)" or the documented real-compose-stack follow-up; report only defects in shipped behaviour or tests that can pass while the spec is violated.

findings.title: Theme guard invariant 1 misses the computed-key custom-property idiom the design system itself uses
findings.evidence: TOKEN_WRITE is `/--[\w-]+['"`]?\s*:|setProperty\(\s*['"`]--/`, so it needs the colon right after the name or its closing quote. The vendored design system sets tokens with `style: { ['--dk-accent' as string]: color }` (src/design-system/components/core.tsx:40). In app code, `style={{ ['--paper' as string]: '#000' }}` or `style={{ [`--paper`]: x }}` has `as string]` or `]` before the colon, so it does not match. `const v = '--paper'; el.style.setProperty(v, '#000')` does not match either. None of these strings contains dark/light/theme, so invariants 2 and 3 miss them too. The test passes while the spec's 'no app source SHALL … declare or set a CSS custom property' is broken, and the most likely way a feature slice would copy the pattern (from core.tsx) is the one that gets through.
findings.suggestion: Match the token name instead of the declaration syntax. In .ts/.tsx, flag any string or template literal that starts with `--` (e.g. /(['"`])--[\w-]/). In .css, flag `--name` followed by optional whitespace or comments and then `:`. Add `['--paper' as string]: x`, `[`--paper`]: x` and `const v='--paper'; setProperty(v, …)` to the `forced` list.

findings.title: Scheme-word check cannot see a scheme word inside a multi-line string or template literal
findings.evidence:
SCHEME_WORD's body is `(?:(?!\1)[^
\]|\.)*?`, so a match cannot cross a newline. In a multi-line className template such as `className={`
  card
  dark
`}`, the opening backtick ends its line and `dark` sits on a line with no quote before it, so invariant 3 does not fire. The doc comment says the invariant holds 'however it is built or applied', but this common way of formatting class templates gets through. Invariants 1 and 2 do not cover a plain class name.
findings.suggestion: Parse literals with the TypeScript scanner or ts-morph, or at least let template literals span newlines (use `[^\\]` instead of `[^\n\\]` when the quote is a backtick). Add a multi-line template case to `forced`.

findings.title: Theme guard scans only .ts/.tsx/.css, not other files Vite bundles
findings.evidence: `sources()` keeps only `/\.(tsx?|css)$/`. A `.js`/`.jsx`/`.mjs` module, or a `.scss`/`.html` partial under src/ that the app imports, would be bundled but never checked, so a `data-theme` write or `--paper:` override there passes the static backstop. The spec scope is 'no app source outside the vendored design system'.
findings.suggestion: Either check every text file under src/ except the vendored and generated trees, or fail the test when src/ has a source file with an extension it does not check.

findings.title: Intl exemption also skips Intl.Segmenter (and other non-ListFormat methods) that take display text
findings.evidence: `if (kind && kind !== "ListFormat") return [];` exempts every method of every Intl object except ListFormat. `Intl.Segmenter.prototype.segment('Ahoj')` returns the given text in segments, so `{[...new Intl.Segmenter('cs').segment('Ahoj')].map(s => s.segment)}` puts the literal on screen without a report. The rule comment claims only ListFormat formats the strings it is given.
findings.suggestion: Turn the logic around: exempt only methods known to take non-text arguments (NumberFormat/DateTimeFormat/RelativeTimeFormat/PluralRules format*, select*, DisplayNames.of) and check the arguments of everything else, including Segmenter.segment. Add a Segmenter case to the invalid list.

findings.title: Container smoke records a clean tree when git status fails
findings.evidence: `dirty: spawnSync('git', ['status', '--porcelain', '--', '.', ':!docs/qa', …]).stdout.trim() !== ''` ignores the exit status. If git exits non-zero (pathspec error, safe.directory refusal, not a repo), stdout is empty, so `dirty` is false and the evidence says 'Tested: commit …' with no uncommitted-changes caveat. If git cannot be spawned, stdout is null and `.trim()` throws before any evidence is written. The evidence-to-commit tie that round 6 added can therefore claim clean without having checked.
findings.suggestion: Check `status === 0` (and `error`) for both git calls. If either fails, mark the run as not tied to a commit (e.g. 'unknown') or exit non-zero instead of defaulting to clean.

findings.title: Theme guard invariant 1 misses a computed-key CSS custom property in a style object
findings.evidence: TOKEN_WRITE is /--[\w-]+['"`]?\s*:|setProperty\(\s*['"`]--/. With a computed key, `<div style={{ ['--paper']: '#000' } as CSSProperties}>`, the text after `--paper'` is `]:`, not `:`, so the regex does not match. SCHEME_API and SCHEME_WORD don't match either, because no string names a scheme. A later slice could write this to override `--paper` or `--ink` on a wrapper. Both theme-source tests would still pass, while the spec delta says app code SHALL NOT 'declare or set a CSS custom property'. The e2e only checks the background on reachable states, so it won't catch an override on an inner element or on a state it doesn't reach. That gap is exactly what this static check was rebuilt to cover.
findings.suggestion: Allow an optional closing bracket before the colon, e.g. /--[\w-]+['"`]?\]?\s*:/. Simpler: flag any string literal that starts with `--` anywhere in app code, and also flag setProperty with a non-literal first argument. Add `{ ['--paper']: '#000' }` to the `forced` probe list.

findings.title: Theme guard skips any src/ directory whose name starts with 'design-system' or 'api/generated'
findings.evidence: sources() uses `p.startsWith('src/design-system')` with no trailing slash, so it skips every path with that prefix. That includes app directories such as `src/design-system-overrides/` or `src/design-system-extras/` as well as the vendored folder. A CSS file there with `:root { --paper: #000 }`, or a component that sets `data-theme`, would force a theme while 'no app source or index.html breaks an invariant' still passes. ESLint's globalIgnores('src/design-system') matches only that exact directory, so the two exemptions don't line up, and the check is weaker than the spec's 'outside the vendored design system'.
findings.suggestion: Compare whole path segments: `p === 'src/design-system' || p.startsWith('src/design-system/')`, and do the same for src/api/generated. Add a unit probe for a sibling directory with the same prefix.

findings.title: Lint rule exempts every Intl formatter method except ListFormat, including Intl.Segmenter.segment, which returns its input text
findings.evidence:
Round 6 skips the arguments of any method on an `Intl.X(...)` / `new Intl.X(...)` receiver unless X is ListFormat. The comment's premise ('methods of an Intl formatter take numbers, dates and identifiers') is wrong for Intl.Segmenter, whose segment(text) returns pieces of the literal it is given. `

{[...new Intl.Segmenter('cs', { granularity: 'word' }).segment('Ahoj světe')].map((s) => s.segment)}

` puts Czech literal text on screen, and the rule reports nothing. That breaks the spec requirement that the rule refuse literal UI text it can see in call arguments. The pseudo-catalog render only catches it if the code runs on a registered route.
findings.suggestion: Use an allow-list of formatter kinds whose methods take no text (NumberFormat, DateTimeFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, PluralRules, DisplayNames, Collator, DurationFormat) instead of a deny-list containing only ListFormat. Any other Intl kind, Segmenter included, then keeps its arguments checked. Add an invalid case for Segmenter.segment('Ahoj').

findings.title: Theme guard invariant 1 ('declares or sets a CSS custom property') misses a token name held in a variable or a computed key
findings.evidence: Spec (No toggle / Theme follows the OS): "No app source outside the vendored design system SHALL … declare or set a CSS custom property"; the No-toggle scenario says that on a route with no control "the static source check covers it" (every current route has no control, so all no-toggle e2e tests skip and this regex is the only check). TOKEN_WRITE = /--[\w-]+['"`]?\s*:|setProperty\(\s*['"`]--/ needs either a colon right after the name (one optional quote allowed) or a quote right after `setProperty(`. These all slip through: `const token = '--paper'; el.style.setProperty(token, '#000')` (`'--paper';` has no colon, and setProperty gets an identifier); `style={{ ['--paper']: '#000' }}` and `style={{ [`--paper`]: x }}` (`']` comes before the colon). Each one overrides the dark/light `--paper` token and so forces a theme, with no scheme word and no scheme API involved, so neither of the other two invariants fires. The 'forced' probe list in the test only has the literal forms the regex already handles.
findings.suggestion: Make invariant 1 hold for any string literal that starts with `--`: flag `(['"`])--[\w-]` anywhere in app code (the `var(--x)` reads in CSS have no quote, so they stay allowed). In TS/TSX, also reject `setProperty(` with any first argument. Add the variable-name and computed-key cases to the `forced` probes.

findings.title: Invariant 3 (no string literal naming a scheme) cannot see a multi-line template literal
findings.evidence:
Spec: no app source SHALL "name a scheme in a string literal". SCHEME_WORD's body is `(?:(?!\1)[^
\]|\.)*?`, which excludes newlines, so the open and close quote must be on the same line. `const cls = `
  dark
`; root.className = cls;` is a string literal naming a scheme, but the line holding `dark` has no quote, so nothing matches. It also hits no other invariant (no `--`, no scheme API). The design calls this check 'however it is built or applied', and the test gives no visible sign of the gap.
findings.suggestion: Let template-literal bodies span newlines (e.g. allow `\n` inside the class when the delimiter is a backtick), or tokenize with the TypeScript scanner and test each string or template token. Add a multi-line template to the `forced` probes.

findings.title: Theme guard skips app files that are not .ts/.tsx/.css and everything under public/
findings.evidence: `sources()` keeps only `/\.(tsx?|css)$/` under `src/`, plus `index.html`. A `public/override.css` declaring `:root{--paper:#000}` and linked from index.html, or any .js/.jsx/.mjs/.scss file a later slice adds under src/, is never read. Yet the requirement covers "No app source outside the vendored design system".
findings.suggestion: Scan every text file under `src/` (minus the design system and generated code), `public/` and `index.html`, or state in the spec which file types are covered.

findings.title: Catalog exemption from the scheme-word invariant is in design.md but not in the spec requirement
findings.evidence: The spec says no app source SHALL "name a scheme in a string literal", with no exception. design.md and theme-source.test.ts (`CATALOGS`, `isCatalog` skips invariant 3) exempt src/i18n/cs.ts and en.ts. So a catalog value such as 'dark' fed into `className={t('x')}` passes the static guard.
findings.suggestion: Amend the spec to name the catalog exception and its rationale. Or keep the catalogs in scope for values used as attributes, e.g. require that catalog values never equal a bare scheme word.

findings.title: Lint rule exempts every Intl method except ListFormat, including Intl.Segmenter.segment(text), which passes text through
findings.evidence: Spec (Literal text is a lint error): the rule refuses literal UI text in "call arguments". The round-6 code is `const kind = intlConstructor(node.callee.object); if (kind && kind !== "ListFormat") return [];`. It is a denylist of one, but `Intl.Segmenter#segment('Ahoj')` also returns the input text as segments. So `[...new Intl.Segmenter('cs').segment('Ahoj')].map((s) => s.segment).join('')` renders 'Ahoj' with no lint error.
findings.suggestion: Turn the exemption around: exempt only methods known to take non-text input (NumberFormat/DateTimeFormat/RelativeTimeFormat/PluralRules format*/select, DisplayNames.of, Collator.compare). Keep checking ListFormat and Segmenter arguments, and add a Segmenter invalid case.

findings.title: Container-smoke dirty flag ignores gitignored files that are still in the Docker build context
findings.evidence: The comment says "every other file is an input", but `git status --porcelain` does not list ignored files. .gitignore ignores `*.log`, `.idea/`, `uploads/`, `storage/`, `**/raw/`, `*.dump` and `src/api/generated/`, and none of these is in .dockerignore, so `COPY . .` puts them in the image. A gitignored file under src/ (e.g. `src/raw/x.ts`) can change the built image while the evidence still says `dirty: false` and ties the result to the commit alone.
findings.suggestion: Add `--ignored` (keeping the generated-evidence exclusions and src/api/generated, which the build regenerates), or align .dockerignore with .gitignore so ignored files never reach the build context.

findings.title: Task 4.1 'qa:verify green' is ticked, but the battery evidence predates the round-6 changes
findings.evidence: tasks.md: "- [x] 4.1 `npm run qa:verify` green." docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md was last committed in 4c1aece (round 5). Its run shows 'Started: 2026-10-04T07:50:58Z'. Commit 184ba12 (10:54Z) then rewrote src/app/theme-source.test.ts, eslint-rules/no-literal-ui-text.js and src/test/lint-rule.test.ts. No lint, unit or coverage battery run covers the shipped rule and tests. Only container-smoke (Playwright through nginx) was re-run at 184ba12. Under the done-claims-need-evidence rule, the tick has no fresh evidence.
findings.suggestion: Re-run `npm run qa:verify` at HEAD and commit the regenerated docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md, or untick 4.1 until that is done.

In that case the file claims a real commit SHA with no caveat. The code is still wrong to treat a failed git call as a clean tree, which goes against the repo's own rule against claims without evidence. Minor severity fits.
